meta.titre: Organic Chemistry: alkanes, alkenes and alcohols

sections.contenu_markdown: Palm wine tapped near Bafoussam turns sour within a day, cooking gas heats the stove in a Yaounde kitchen, and the plastic bag that carries the fish from the market is made from a gas obtained from petroleum. All these are organic compounds, compounds of carbon, and they fall into a few families with very regular behaviour. In the GCE O/L you are expected to define a homologous series, name and write the first members of the alkanes, alkenes and alcohols, and describe their main reactions. Once you know the pattern of one reaction of each family, you can write the others.

items: Carbon atoms form four covalent bonds.
Crude oil is a mixture of hydrocarbons separated by fractional distillation.
A balanced equation has the same number of atoms of each element on both sides.
Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon gives carbon dioxide and water.

sections.titre: Homologous series: alkanes, alkenes and alcohols
sections.contenu_markdown:
Organic chemistry is the chemistry of carbon compounds. A **hydrocarbon** contains only carbon and hydrogen.

A **homologous series** is a family of organic compounds that have the **same general formula**, the **same functional group** and similar chemical properties. Neighbouring members differ by a $\mathrm{CH_2}$ unit, and their physical properties, such as boiling point, change gradually along the series.

| Series | General formula | Functional group | First members |
|---|---|---|---|
| Alkanes | $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+2}}$ | only C-C single bonds (saturated) | methane $\mathrm{CH_{4}}$, ethane $\mathrm{C_{2}H_{6}}$, propane $\mathrm{C_{3}H_{8}}$, butane $\mathrm{C_{4}H_{10}}$ |
| Alkenes | $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n}}$ | C=C double bond (unsaturated) | ethene $\mathrm{C_{2}H_{4}}$, propene $\mathrm{C_{3}H_{6}}$, butene $\mathrm{C_{4}H_{8}}$ |
| Alcohols | $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+1}OH}$ | -OH group | methanol $\mathrm{CH_{3}OH}$, ethanol $\mathrm{C_{2}H_{5}OH}$, propan-1-ol $\mathrm{C_{3}H_{7}OH}$ |
| Carboxylic acids | $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+1}COOH}$ | -COOH group | methanoic acid $\mathrm{HCOOH}$, ethanoic acid $\mathrm{CH_{3}COOH}$ |

The stem of the name shows the number of carbon atoms: meth- (1), eth- (2), prop- (3), but- (4), pent- (5), hex- (6).

**Two types of reaction to know**

- **Substitution:** one atom is replaced by another. It is typical of alkanes.
- **Addition:** a molecule adds across a double bond and only one product forms. It is typical of alkenes.

All hydrocarbons burn. In plenty of air they give carbon dioxide and water, for example $\mathrm{CH_{4}\ +\ 2O_{2}  \rightarrow  CO_{2}\ +\ 2H_{2}O}$; in a limited supply of air they give carbon monoxide or soot.

variantes.quand_utiliser: A question asks for a substitution reaction or the reactivity of alkanes.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Alkanes are saturated and fairly unreactive. In ultraviolet light or sunlight, methane reacts with chlorine: $\mathrm{CH_{4}\ +\ Cl_{2}  \rightarrow  CH_{3}Cl\ +\ HCl}$. A hydrogen atom has been **replaced** by a chlorine atom, so this is a substitution reaction; the reaction can continue until all hydrogen atoms are replaced. Alkanes do not decolourise bromine water.

variantes.quand_utiliser: A question asks about the test for unsaturation or the reactions of ethene.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Ethene adds to bromine: $\mathrm{C_{2}H_{4}\ +\ Br_{2}  \rightarrow  C_{2}H_{4}Br_{2}}$. The orange-brown bromine water becomes **colourless**: this is the test for a C=C double bond. With hydrogen and a nickel catalyst: $\mathrm{C_{2}H_{4}\ +\ H_{2}  \rightarrow  C_{2}H_{6}}$. With steam and a catalyst (phosphoric acid) at high temperature and pressure: $\mathrm{C_{2}H_{4}\ +\ H_{2}O  \rightarrow  C_{2}H_{5}OH}$. Alkenes are made by **cracking**, in which large alkane molecules are broken into smaller molecules: $\mathrm{C_{10}H_{22}  \rightarrow  C_{8}H_{18}\ +\ C_{2}H_{4}}$. Ethene is also the monomer of polythene.

variantes.quand_utiliser: A question asks for the source or a use of ethanol, or its reactions.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Ethanol is made by **fermentation** of sugars (for example in palm wine or sugar cane juice) by the enzymes in yeast, without air at about 25 to 35 °C: $\mathrm{C_{6}H_{12}O_{6}  \rightarrow  2C_{2}H_{5}OH\ +\ 2CO_{2}}$. It is also made from ethene and steam. Uses: solvent (perfumes, varnish), fuel, antiseptic and alcoholic drinks. It burns: $\mathrm{C_{2}H_{5}OH\ +\ 3O_{2}  \rightarrow  2CO_{2}\ +\ 3H_{2}O}$. It is oxidised by air (with bacteria) or by acidified potassium dichromate(VI) to ethanoic acid, and reacts with ethanoic acid with concentrated sulphuric acid as catalyst to form the ester ethyl ethanoate, which has a fruity smell: $\mathrm{C_{2}H_{5}OH\ +\ CH_{3}COOH  \rightleftharpoons  CH_{3}COOC_{2}H_{5}\ +\ H_{2}O}$.

sections.enonce_markdown: Palm wine contains ethanol formed from the sugar glucose: $\mathrm{C_{6}H_{12}O_{6}  \rightarrow  2C_{2}H_{5}OH\ +\ 2CO_{2}}$. A sugary juice contains 90 g of glucose, which is completely fermented. (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16; molar volume = 24 $\mathrm{dm^3}$.) State the conditions needed for fermentation, then calculate (a) the mass of ethanol and (b) the volume of carbon dioxide formed at room temperature and pressure.

etapes.justification: Fermentation uses enzymes in yeast, which work best at moderate temperature and without air.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Yeast, a temperature of about 25 to 35 °C, and no oxygen (air).

etapes.justification: The ratio glucose : ethanol is 1 : 2 and $M(\mathrm{C_2H_5OH}) = 46\ \mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$.

etapes.action: Find the volume of carbon dioxide.
etapes.justification: The ratio glucose : carbon dioxide is also 1 : 2 and 1 mol of gas occupies 24 dm$^3$.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The fermentation of 90 g of glucose gives **46 g of ethanol** and **24 dm$^3$ of carbon dioxide**.

items.erreur_markdown: The general formula of the alkenes is $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+2}}$.
items.pourquoi_faux: That is the general formula of the alkanes. An alkene has a double bond, so it has two fewer hydrogen atoms.

items.erreur_markdown: Ethene reacts with bromine by substitution and gives off hydrogen bromide.
items.pourquoi_faux: Ethene is unsaturated and the bromine molecule adds across the double bond, so only one product forms.
items.correction_markdown: $\mathrm{C_{2}H_{4}\ +\ Br_{2}  \rightarrow  C_{2}H_{4}Br_{2}}$ is an addition reaction. Substitution is typical of alkanes.

items.pourquoi_faux: Propane is saturated and has no double bond for bromine to add to.
items.correction_markdown: Only unsaturated compounds such as alkenes decolourise bromine water.

items.erreur_markdown: Members of a homologous series are compounds that differ by one carbon atom.
items.pourquoi_faux: Neighbouring members differ by a $\mathrm{CH_2}$ unit (one carbon and two hydrogen atoms), and they must also share the general formula and the functional group.
items.correction_markdown: A homologous series has the same general formula and functional group, similar chemical properties and members that differ by $\mathrm{CH_2}$.

items.erreur_markdown: Fermentation of sugar to ethanol needs a lot of oxygen from the air.
items.pourquoi_faux: Fermentation is done without air. With oxygen the ethanol is oxidised to ethanoic acid, which is how palm wine turns sour.
items.correction_markdown: Keep air out and use yeast at about 25 to 35 °C.

items.enonce_markdown:
Write the molecular formula of:

(a) the alkane with five carbon atoms

(b) the alkene with four carbon atoms

(c) the alcohol with three carbon atoms

(d) Name the alkane with the formula $\mathrm{C_{3}H_{8}}$.

Complete and balance each equation, and state the type of reaction.

(a) Propane burns completely in air.

(b) Ethene reacts with hydrogen in the presence of a nickel catalyst.

(c) Methane reacts with chlorine in sunlight to form chloromethane and one other product.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) $\mathrm{C_{3}H_{8}\ +\ 5O_{2}  \rightarrow  3CO_{2}\ +\ 4H_{2}O}$ (combustion, an oxidation reaction)

(b) $\mathrm{C_{2}H_{4}\ +\ H_{2}  \rightarrow  C_{2}H_{6}}$ (addition)

(c) $\mathrm{CH_{4}\ +\ Cl_{2}  \rightarrow  CH_{3}Cl\ +\ HCl}$ (substitution; the other product is hydrogen chloride)

items.enonce_markdown:
A sample of 14.2 g of decane, $\mathrm{C_{10}H_{22}}$, is cracked completely into octane and ethene: $\mathrm{C_{10}H_{22}  \rightarrow  C_{8}H_{18}\ +\ C_{2}H_{4}}$. (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16; molar volume = 24 $\mathrm{dm^3}$.)

(a) Calculate the volume of ethene formed at room temperature and pressure.

(b) All the ethene is converted to ethanol by reaction with steam. Write the equation and calculate the mass of ethanol.

(c) Describe a test that shows the product of cracking is unsaturated and give the result.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) $M(\mathrm{C_{10}H_{22}}) = 120 + 22 = 142$, so $n = \dfrac{14.2}{142} = 0.10\ \mathrm{mol}$. The ratio decane : ethene is 1 : 1, so $V = 0.10 \times 24 = $ **2.4 dm$^3$**.

(b) $\mathrm{C_{2}H_{4}\ +\ H_{2}O  \rightarrow  C_{2}H_{5}OH}$. The ratio is 1 : 1, so $n(\mathrm{C_2H_5OH}) = 0.10\ \mathrm{mol}$ and $m = 0.10 \times 46 = $ **4.6 g**.

(c) Shake the gas with bromine water: the orange-brown colour turns **colourless**, which shows a C=C double bond.

items_markdown: A homologous series has the same general formula and functional group, similar chemical properties and members differing by $\mathrm{CH_2}$.
Alkanes $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+2}}$ are saturated and undergo substitution with chlorine in sunlight.
Alkenes $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n}}$ contain C=C, undergo addition, and decolourise bromine water.
Alcohols $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+1}OH}$: ethanol is made by fermentation (yeast, no air, 25 to 35 °C) or from ethene and steam.
Ethanol is used as a solvent, a fuel and in drinks; it oxidises to ethanoic acid and forms esters with acids.
